title: Deepest lakes
measure: Maximum depth in metres, from the surface to the deepest known point. Includes the Caspian Sea, which geographers usually class as a lake, and Lake Vostok, which lies under the Antarctic ice. Ranked by maximum depth, not average depth. Where the lake's managing body has published a survey, that figure is used.

entries.name: Baikal
entries.note: Also the largest freshwater lake by volume. Guinness World Records lists the same 1,642 m.
entries.source: Guinness World Records, Deepest lake; Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth

entries.name: Tanganyika
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: Caspian Sea
entries.note: Called a sea, but generally classed by geographers and limnologists as a huge inland salt lake.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: O'Higgins / San Martín
entries.note: The deepest lake in the Americas.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: Vostok
entries.location: Under the East Antarctic Ice Sheet
entries.note: Sealed under about 4 km of Antarctic ice. Seismic mapping by Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory found about 800 m of water in its southern basin and about 400 m in the northern one. Published estimates of its deepest point range from 510 m to 900 m.
entries.source: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory seismic survey, via SpaceNews; Christner and Priscu, Encyclopedia of Water; Wikipedia, Lake Vostok

entries.name: Argentino
entries.note: Not in the National Park Service list or many older top 10s, but included in Wikipedia's current list.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Malawi
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: Issyk-Kul
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: Great Slave
entries.note: The deepest lake in North America.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth; US National Park Service, The World's Deepest Lakes (2017)

entries.name: Crater Lake
entries.note: Measured with multibeam sonar in 2000. Some lists give 594 m. Lake Matano in Indonesia (590 m) is just 2 m behind.
entries.source: US National Park Service, Crater Lake (2000 multibeam sonar survey)
